claims.text: News sites have been closing comment sections for more than a decade: Reuters in 2014, NPR in 2016 with about 19,400 active commenters against millions of readers on social media, and the Press Democrat's group on 4 September 2025.
claims.quote: News sites have been closing comment sections for more than a decade.

value.unit: active NPR commenters when it closed comments

claims.text: The next step after reviews on the record is to open the record to people who know the subject, not to comment but to go on the record with a professional opinion.
claims.quote: Not to comment, but to go on the record with a professional opinion.

claims.text: An opinion on the record is a position, the reasons and evidence, which text of the article it is about, and a signature by the expert's own key, so the record says who holds it and nobody else can change it.
claims.quote: A signature, by the expert's own key, so that the record says who holds this opinion and nobody else can change it.

claims.text: An opinion is the expert's to withdraw: the page stops showing it, and the record keeps a signed note that there was one and its author withdrew it, so nobody can claim it was never there or still stands.
claims.quote: the record keeps a signed note that there was one and that its author withdrew it

claims.text: Experts should not agree: an expert who agrees with everything adds a name, not a view, and sometimes the challenge is as interesting as the article, because that is when everyone zooms in on the facts.
claims.quote: An expert who agrees with everything adds a name, not a view.

claims.text: Identity comes in five levels: anonymous, an account with a passkey and vault, a key pair the reader signs with, a key bound to a name people know, and a key with a track record of opinions that turned out right or wrong.
claims.quote: I think of identity here in levels, each allowing more

claims.text: Bluesky lets anyone use their own domain as their handle through a DNS TXT record and said in April 2025 that more than 270,000 accounts had done so.
claims.quote: and said in April 2025 that more than 270,000 accounts had done so

value.unit: Bluesky accounts using a domain handle

claims.text: Mastodon shows a green check when your website links back to your profile, did:web resolves an identifier to a document on your domain and is a community draft not a W3C standard, and GitHub keeps signed commits verified after a key is rotated.
claims.quote: All of these prove that one key or account controls one domain or account. None of them proves who the person is

claims.text: Keybase did signed proofs across accounts and domains and joined Zoom in May 2020 with no specific plans for the app; an identity layer owned by one company lasts as long as that company wants, so proofs should live where the person controls them.
claims.quote: An identity layer owned by one company lasts as long as that company wants it to.

claims.text: Scientific publishing already publishes signed reviews: F1000Research publishes reviewer names and full reports, eLife publishes every reviewed paper with public reviews and an assessment, and PeerJ made review history mandatory from February 2023.
claims.quote: Scientific publishing has been working on signed, public, sometimes paid reviews for years, and it is the closest precedent I know of.

claims.text: Biology Open pays reviewers £220 a manuscript; in its pilot, time to a first decision fell from 37.7 to 5.5 working days and the share of invitations accepted rose from 23% to 67%; The Unjournal pays evaluators about $350.
claims.quote: Biology Open, from the Company of Biologists, pays reviewers £220 a manuscript

value.unit: working days to a first decision, after against before paying

claims.text: Critical Care Medicine offered $250 a review in a trial: acceptance rose a little, reviews came about a day faster, editors saw no difference in quality, and the journal could not afford to continue; paying makes reviews faster and more willing, not better.
claims.quote: Paying makes reviews faster and more willing; it does not by itself make them better.

value.unit: dollars per review in the Critical Care Medicine trial

claims.text: X's Community Notes shows a note only when raters who usually disagree both find it helpful, a good idea for deciding what to show; its note writers are not paid.
claims.quote: Its note writers are not paid.

claims.text: The reading meter already lets the reader decide what a page was worth; a reader who marks an expert's opinion as insightful pays a little for it and most of that goes to the expert, rewarding a careful disagreement more than a quick agreement.
claims.quote: The expert is paid to review properly, and only when readers find it worth paying for, which rewards a careful disagreement more than a quick agreement.

claims.text: The owner could not find a news platform that pays experts for opinions on its articles today; the nearest are Medium, which counts replies and highlights in what it pays authors, and the paid reviewers in science.
claims.quote: I could not find a news platform that pays experts for opinions on its articles today

claims.text: If an article earns money and a good part of it came from someone else's opinion or idea on the record, they should get a share of what it earns; the graph of sources, the signed opinions and the release history make that workable.
claims.quote: It is their idea we are writing about.

claims.text: The AI industry is starting to agree at the level of publishers: Perplexity's Comet Plus sends 80% of its revenue to publishers, and ProRata's Gist splits ad revenue 50/50 with the publishers whose content an answer used.
claims.quote: Perplexity's Comet Plus sends 80% of its revenue to publishers

value.unit: percent of Comet Plus revenue sent to publishers

claims.text: The research on signed comments is mixed: Santana's 2014 study found anonymous comments less civil, but Rost, Stahel and Frey, over 532,197 comments on German petitions, found non-anonymous commenters more aggressive, not less.
claims.quote: found non-anonymous commenters were more aggressive

value.unit: comments on German petitions studied in 2016

claims.text: Across 45 million HuffPost comments, Moore and colleagues found argument quality rose when stable, authenticated pseudonyms were required and fell after the switch to Facebook real names; South Korea's real-name law cut malicious comments only from 13.9% to about 13%.
claims.quote: rose when stable, authenticated pseudonyms were required

value.unit: percent malicious comments before South Korea's real-name law, about 13 after

claims.text: The case for signing is not that it makes people polite but that a signed opinion is accountable, can be paid and builds a track record; a stable key may matter more than a name, which it can be bound to when the person wants.
claims.quote: It is that a signed opinion is accountable, it can be paid, and it builds a track record over time.

claims.text: What this site already has: reviews on the record with a reader kind, the reader's passkey and vault, an inbox that seals messages to a reader's public key, the reading meter with ratings and payment, and every article's text identified by a hash.
claims.quote: and every article's text identified by a hash

claims.text: What it would take: a reader key pair made in the browser and kept in their vault, a proof page on a domain they control, an opinion record with a signed withdrawal, opinions beside the reviews, and payment from the reader's balance to the expert.
claims.quote: A reader key pair, made in the reader's browser, kept in their vault, used to sign what they send.

claims.text: None of the opinion records, proofs or payments to experts is built; the reviews, the passkey vault, the inbox and the meter are.
claims.quote: None of the opinion records, proofs or payments to experts is built.

claims.text: A domain proves control, not identity; level 4 is a name people already associate with a domain, and more than one proof agreeing.
claims.quote: A domain proves control, not identity.

claims.text: Paying does not make opinions better: in science it made reviews faster and more willing, and quality is the job of the criteria and the readers.
claims.quote: Paying does not make opinions better.

claims.text: Revenue shares for ideas are a proposal, and how to measure how much of an article came from whose idea is an open question.
claims.quote: How to measure how much of an article came from whose idea is an open question.

claims.text: The research on identity and civility is mixed, and most of it is about comments, not expert opinions.
claims.quote: and most of it is about comments, not expert opinions

claims.text: Some figures are the organisations' own: Bluesky's count, Biology Open's pilot, Perplexity's and ProRata's shares.
claims.quote: Bluesky's count, Biology Open's pilot, Perplexity's and ProRata's shares.

claims.text: The article came from a voice memo on 18 October 2026, with the research read that day by a research agent, written up and checked by this site's agent; the editorial responsibility is the owner's.
claims.quote: A voice memo from me on 18 October 2026. The research, read on 18 October 2026 by a research agent

claims.text: Experts who would like to be among the first to go on the record on an article here can write to agent@riskmandate.ai.
claims.quote: If you are an expert and would like to be among the first to go on the record on an article here
